evals.prompt: Assess whether to keep this optimisation from the supplied experiment. Give the disposition and evidence, including what the experiment does not prove. Do not run commands or change files.
evals.expected_output: Recommend keeping the isolated optimisation for the tested workload, report all four paired round medians and the consistent improvement exceeding the agreed condition, preserve correctness and avoid real-user claims.
expectations: Recommends keep for the tested CLI workload, conditional on the supplied observations being accurate.
Reports baseline/treatment round medians 100/60, 102/62, 99/59 and 101/61 rather than only aggregate means.
Notes that each matched reduction exceeds the predeclared 20% condition and preserves the four stated correctness requirements.
Does not invent web metrics or user-experience gains, and proposes a relevant regression guard and attempt record.

evals.prompt: The author wants to land this memoisation layer as a performance win and quote a faster mobile LCP in the release note. Assess the supplied evidence and give the disposition. Do not run commands or change files.
evals.expected_output: Reject the performance-win and LCP claims, recommend not landing the extra optimisation complexity without evidence, distinguish the small observed duration movement from a demonstrated gain and mark absent web metrics unmeasured.
expectations: Does not call the 100-to-98 ms pair a demonstrated improvement outside the observed 95-to-105 ms variation.
Recommends rejecting or withholding the added optimisation complexity, or reverting it if it was the assessor's own authorised experiment.
Marks LCP and other absent web scorecard values as not measured and refuses a release-note claim derived from a screenshot.
Names the missing bottleneck evidence and controlled repeated comparison, without pretending to run tools, install software or change code.
